subject: Realtime chat: elevated latency observed — coordination and mitigations
messages:
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime chat: elevated latency observed — coordination and mitigations

Hi Jane / Tim —

I wanted to reach out quickly to acknowledge the high-latency behavior you reported on the live chat/streaming endpoint this morning (we see the same spike in our telemetry). First: we’re sorry — this disruption clearly impacted interactive sessions during your morning peak and we know that’s critical for FastRetail’s checkout chat flows.

What we know so far:
- Between 07:45–08:30 PT we observed a token-delivery latency increase across a subset of us-west serving nodes, correlated with an increase in long-running KV cache misses.
- The impact manifested as delayed first-chunk delivery and intermittent 'stuttering' of message tokens for sessions routed to affected hosts.
- Your SRE report included helpful traces (thank you) — we’ve attached a short telemetry snippet and will share the full extraction in the drive link.

Immediate next steps we’re executing now:
1) Traffic routing: we’ve shifted your requests to an alternate shard set with identical model variants; this provides immediate mitigation for new sessions.
2) Circuit mitigation: increased short-term autoscaling headroom for your Dedicated pool to reduce queueing.
3) Client guidance: see the mitigation checklist attached — it includes temporary client-side backoff and a recommended retry window (250ms initial, exponential to 2s).

We’ll keep you updated on root cause analysis. For now, can you confirm whether you observed errors for specific regions or only US-west? Also: if you can send any additional traces or a representative session id, that will speed triage.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie —

We appreciate the quick acknowledgement. We saw the issue in two of our primary checkout regions (us-west and us-east) — us-west was worse. Symptoms were: delayed initial messages (1–3s), followed by token bursts when the stream recovered. Attached is one session id and the corresponding client-side trace.

Session id: fr-cc-20261025-34a7
Client trace: included via paste (large) — will share ETA on full logs.

Two asks for your team:
1) If routing to another shard set is the short-term fix, can you confirm whether that requires a client restart or if it will be transparent? We have 300 active sockets; a transparent fix would be ideal.
2) We need an ETA for a post-incident summary and whether any credits/SLA remediation will be considered given the impact window.

Tim — looping you in for our internal ops follow-up.

— Jane
Jane Doe
Product Lead, Conversational Commerce — FastRetail
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Realtime chat: elevated latency observed — coordination and mitigations

Jane / Tim / Stephanie —

Thanks for the context, Jane. Quick technical update and practical mitigation steps from the ops side: 

Rooted triage so far (in-progress):
- Initial signal points to an emergent interaction between our cache eviction policy and the tail-latency path for long-running KV state when sequence lengths exceed typical checkout prompts. A small subset of host kernels entered a degraded path that increased per-token scheduling latency.
- We have a concurrent ticket open (INF-4821) to track the kernel hotfix and scheduler tuning.

Short-term mitigations already applied (effective immediately):
- Transparent routing: we forced a routing rebalancing. This is transparent for existing sockets for most clients; however, a small proportion of long-lived WS connections will see a short reconnect. We minimized impact by draining connections rather than hard drop.
- Autoscale headroom: +20% capacity reserved for FastRetail in your Dedicated pool for the next 3 hours.
- Token pacing suggestion: for critical flows, add a 150ms jitter between chunk reads to de-synchronize client bursts; our attached checklist has code snippets.

Action items for our teams:
- Redwood (ben/infra): push scheduler tuning to canary within 4 hours; full roll to affected fleet in 24–36 hours pending validation.
- Redwood (marissa): prepare a concise postmortem and impact window for FastRetail; include request/response percentiles and representative traces.
- FastRetail (Tim): if you can share 3 representative connection ids, we’ll prioritize their traces.

Regarding credits/SLA:Stephanie will coordinate commercial follow-up. We will quantify the impact window and provide an estimate for any customer relief under the SLA after our postmortem.

Attaching a short mitigation checklist PDF that you can share with your engineers.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Jane / Tim —

Thank you for the quick signals and the session id. To summarize next steps and SLAs: 

1) Operational: Ben’s team will run the canary scheduler tuning and we expect a full fleet rollout only after validation (target: 24–36 hours). I’ll share the canary results as they complete.
2) Client guidance: The mitigation checklist (attached) includes sample WS reconnect logic and token pacing snippets; earlier routing changes are transparent for most connections but we recommend an orchestrated reconnect for critical sessions during a quiet window.
3) Postmortem & SLA: Marissa will deliver a post-incident summary within 48 hours with an impact table (sessions affected, error rates, duration). After the postmortem, our customer success team will propose any appropriate account remediation/credits per your contract (FR-2026-Q4-0911).

If acceptable I’d like to schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through the postmortem draft and immediate actions. Please reply with availability.

Appreciate your partnership — we’ll get this stabilized.

Best,
